cosy-lesson.title: Why Do I Feel Like Everyone Is Copying Me?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Mimic – to imitate someone or their actions, especially in order to entertain or ridicule.

p.em: Example: She noticed her coworkers starting to mimic her unique vocabulary and expressions.

cosy-blockquote.p: Flattery – excessive and insincere praise, given especially to further one's own interests.

p.em: Example: They say imitation is the highest form of flattery, but it can feel incredibly annoying.

cosy-blockquote.p: Plagiarize – to take the work or an idea of someone else and pass it off as one's own.

p.em: Example: It is rude when a close friend tries to plagiarize your signature style.
Example: In a sea of replica styles, maintaining an authentic voice is the ultimate challenge.

cosy-blockquote.p: Trendsetter – a person who leads the way in fashion or ideas.

p.em: Example: She was a natural trendsetter, always wearing boots months before they became popular.

cosy-blockquote.p: Identity – the fact of being who or what a person is.

p.em: Example: Replicating someone else's drink preferences feels like stealing a piece of their identity.

cosy-blockquote.p: Clone – an exact copy of a person or thing.

p.em: Example: Walking into the party, she realized everyone had dressed like a clone of her.

cosy-blockquote.p: Influence – the capacity to have an effect on the character, development, or behavior of someone.

p.em: Example: She didn't realize her choice of jazz music would have such a strong influence on the group.

cosy-blockquote.p: Unique – being the only one of its kind; unlike anything else.

p.em: Example: Everyone wants to feel unique, but we are all influenced by the same popular culture.

cosy-blockquote.p: Insecurity – uncertainty or anxiety about oneself; lack of confidence.

p.em: Example: Copying another person's outfit often stems from a deep personal insecurity.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
Why do close friends often feel the urge to mimic our personal style, from our shoe choices to our conversational quirks?
★ Have you ever noticed someone copying your specific mannerisms or way of speaking?

When someone replicates your signature drink or outfit, does it feel like a genuine flattery or a frustrating boundary crossing?
★ How do you react when someone takes credit for an idea you introduced?

Is it possible to completely plagiarize another person's lifestyle, or is there always a part of the original that remains untamed?
★ Have you ever felt that a friend was trying to plagiarize your entire personality?

How do we define what is truly authentic in a culture completely saturated by viral social media aesthetics?
★ What is the most authentic and un-copyable part of your daily routine?

Does being a natural trendsetter in your social circle come with a sense of pride or a burden of constant reinvention?
★ Are you usually the first among your friends to discover new music, fashion, or local venues?

Why do we tie so much of our personal identity to external consumer choices like drinks, music preferences, and outfit styles?
★ What is one signature item or hobby that you feel represents your identity best?

In a world of fast-fashion and algorithm-driven playlists, are we all just becoming sophisticated versions of a social clone?
★ Have you ever walked into an event and realized someone was wearing the exact same outfit as you?

How do you measure the boundary between healthy artistic influence and outright, uncreative replication?
★ Who has had the biggest influence on your tastes in music, film, or literature?

Why does our desire to be unique often conflict with our deep-seated human need to belong to a community?
★ What is a quirky preference of yours that you are certain is completely unique to you?

Is the need to copy another person's lifestyle choices a sign of admiration, or does it stem from deep social insecurity?
★ Have you ever copied someone else's style because you were unsure of your own?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
Modern social media has turned personal style into an easily-cloned aesthetic, forcing us to mimic viral trends to feel included.
★ Do you feel that social media has made everyone's personal style look identical?

In older times, imitation was the sincerest form of flattery; today, modern hyper-individualism makes us view copying as an offense.
★ Have you ever felt frustrated when a friend bought the exact same item or copied your style?

We fear that copycats will plagiarize our lifestyle, a self-conscious worry that traditional community members never experienced.
★ Have you ever felt that a friend was trying to plagiarize your entire personality?

In a world completely saturated by digital templates, finding an authentic lifestyle has become a highly exhausting modern pursuit.
★ What is the most authentic and un-copyable part of your daily routine?

Older generations relied on localized, enduring traditions, while modern people must constantly act as a trendsetter to maintain social value.
★ Are you usually the first among your friends to discover new music, fashion, or local venues?

We tie our personal identity to external consumer choices, unlike past eras where identity was rooted in heritage and labor.
★ What is one signature item or hobby that you feel represents your identity best?

Modern fast-fashion has made it incredibly cheap to become a social clone, destroying the unique, manual craftsmanship of the past.
★ Have you ever walked into an event and realized someone was wearing the exact same outfit as you?

Older generations valued the deep, lifetime influence of mentors, while modern youth are guided by fleeting algorithmic recommendations.
★ Who has had the biggest influence on your tastes in music, film, or literature?

In traditional societies, social conformity was a unique virtue; today, we are obsessed with being completely different from everyone else.
★ What is a quirky preference of yours that you are certain is completely unique to you?

We copy others because we are terrified of isolation, yet we hate being copied because of our deep modern insecurity about our individuality.
★ Have you ever copied someone else's style because you were unsure of your own?
